name: File Association Hijacking Attempt
description: Detects modification of the command executed when a specific file type is opened. Adversaries can hijack file associations to execute malicious code when a user opens a seemingly benign file.

action.description: The default command for a file association was modified. This could be an attempt to execute malicious code when a user opens a file.

operational_usage: Examine the process making the change and the new command being set. For example, changing the command for '.txt' files from 'notepad.exe' to 'powershell.exe -enc ...' is highly malicious.
false_positive: Can occur when a user legitimately changes their default program for a file type (e.g., switching from Notepad to Notepad++). The context of the process (e.g., user-interactive vs. script) is important for triage.
